title: Operator manifest
description: Describes one job the data model can ask an environment to run: what it needs, what it takes, what it produces. An operator knows nothing about who asks or where it runs.

status.description: planned: designed but not implemented; the entrypoint need not exist yet.

entrypoint.description: Run from the root of a checkout of the data model at the requested revision. `{param}` is replaced by the parameter's value; a list parameter expands to one argument per item.

requires.description: Capabilities the environment must have, all of them (e.g. snowflake, databricks, lab, product-tests, artifactory, github, chrome).

credentials.description: Environment variables the job reads, as secrets. Never part of a job request.

python_packages.description: What the interpreter must have installed.

kind.description: model-files: files in the checkout, delivered as a change to the model. artifact: a file or folder published to the artifact store. report: text for the person who asked.

paths.description: Globs relative to the checkout (model-files) or to the work directory (artifact).

release.description: Where the official release of this artifact is published. A release is immutable; model records should point at it rather than at a rebuilt copy.

path.description: Folder in the store; releases are sub-folders named YYYYMMDD-BBB with a manifest.json written last.

used_by.description: Where in the UI this is asked for today.

triggers.description: Globs of model paths whose change makes this operator's output stale. The tracker (in the operators repository) turns a change between two revisions into the runs that need doing; the model's own CI can use the same globs.

trigger_parameter.description: Name of a list parameter that receives the changed paths that matched `triggers`, so a run can be limited to what changed (e.g. the assets that were edited).

capability.description: e.g. snowflake, databricks, lab, product-tests, artifactory, github
